meta.title: Strategic Marketing and Brand Management
meta.description: Access Bank School of Banking Excellence — Entry-Level Training Program quiz covering all five modules: Strategic Marketing & the Customer Value Journey, Targeting Prospects, Decision & Adoption, Advocacy & Brand Management, and Measuring Marketing ROI.

questionBank.q: A bank commits to a long-term, research-driven approach that aligns its products with evolving customer needs, using segmentation and ongoing customer insight. Which term names this approach?
questionBank.ans: Strategic marketing
questionBank.exp: Module 1 defines strategic marketing as the long-term, research-driven approach to aligning products with customer needs. Marketing strategy is short-term and campaign-specific; brand positioning is one tool within strategic marketing, not the whole approach; CRM is a Module 4 post-acquisition concept.

questionBank.q: A bank's leadership decides to reposition itself as the leading choice for diaspora remittances over five years, backed by customer research and segmentation. Which concept best describes this?
questionBank.ans: Practicing strategic marketing
questionBank.exp: A long-term repositioning grounded in research and segmentation is strategic marketing. A short single campaign or a survey are narrower, tactical activities within or feeding into that broader approach.

questionBank.q: Which of the following best exemplifies a marketing strategy rather than strategic marketing?
questionBank.ans: A one-month savings-account promotion campaign
questionBank.exp: Marketing strategy refers to specific, short-term actions and campaigns (mirroring the module's own social-media-campaign example). The other options are all long-term, strategic-marketing-type undertakings.

questionBank.q: A new marketing officer proposes a two-week cashback push timed to a public holiday, aimed only at that month's account openings. Which term describes this initiative?
questionBank.ans: Marketing strategy
questionBank.exp: A short, campaign-specific action tied to an immediate goal is marketing strategy. Strategic marketing, brand equity, and CVJ mapping are all longer-term or broader constructs covered elsewhere in the module.

questionBank.q: A bank sets its overall five-year direction while a separate team runs weekly promotions to hit monthly targets. Which pairing correctly classifies each activity by time frame?
opts: The five-year plan is strategic marketing; the weekly pushes are marketing strategy
The five-year plan is marketing strategy; the weekly pushes are strategic marketing
questionBank.ans: The five-year plan is strategic marketing; the weekly pushes are marketing strategy
questionBank.exp: Strategic marketing carries a long-term vision toward future goals, while marketing strategy covers short-term objectives and actions — matching the module's time-frame distinction.

questionBank.q: Two bank objectives are proposed: sustaining long-term customer relationships, and launching a new product this quarter. Which objective belongs to strategic marketing?
opts: Both belong equally to strategic marketing
questionBank.ans: Sustaining long-term customer relationships
questionBank.exp: Strategic marketing's objective is sustained growth and customer relationships, whereas immediate goals like product launches are the domain of marketing strategy.

questionBank.q: Which approach best characterizes strategic marketing, as opposed to marketing strategy?
opts: Limited to a single advertising channel
questionBank.ans: Customer-centric and research-driven
questionBank.exp: Strategic marketing's approach is customer-centric and research-driven; marketing strategy is described as campaign-specific and tactical, matching the other distractors' flavor.

questionBank.q: A bank wants to position itself as a leader in financial inclusion nationally. A rival instead runs a single social-media push for a new savings account. Which bank is practicing strategic marketing?
opts: The rival running the social-media push
The bank positioning itself as a leader in financial inclusion
questionBank.ans: The bank positioning itself as a leader in financial inclusion
questionBank.exp: Positioning as a market leader mirrors the module's own worked example of strategic marketing; a single social-media promotion mirrors its worked example of marketing strategy.

questionBank.q: An employee wants to build lifetime relationships rather than judge a customer's worth by their opening transaction alone. Which strategic-thinking principle does this reflect?
opts: Focus on lifetime value, not just transactions
questionBank.ans: Focus on lifetime value, not just transactions
questionBank.exp: The lifetime-value principle holds that a customer's true worth is measured over time, not at account opening, achieved through understanding goals, offering relevant solutions, and regular engagement.

questionBank.q: A relationship officer meets a new customer, only tracks their financial goals once, and never follows up again after account opening. Which practice is this officer failing to apply?
opts: Clearly communicating product terms up front
Understanding customer goals and maintaining regular engagement over time
Guiding the customer through digital-banking adoption
Monitoring the account for signs of inactivity
questionBank.ans: Understanding customer goals and maintaining regular engagement over time
questionBank.exp: The lifetime-value principle is built through understanding a customer's financial goals, offering relevant solutions, and maintaining regular engagement — the missing ongoing follow-up is precisely this practice, described here as an action rather than restating the principle's name (contrast with Q9).

questionBank.q: Which action best reflects the principle of ensuring easy and effective onboarding?
opts: Waiting for the customer to request a callback
Guiding a new customer through options and following up on digital-banking adoption
Offering a loan only after two years of account history
Sending a satisfaction survey at year-end
questionBank.ans: Guiding a new customer through options and following up on digital-banking adoption
questionBank.exp: Effective onboarding means guiding customers through their banking options, encouraging digital adoption, and following up to ensure seamless integration into the bank's ecosystem.

questionBank.q: A newly onboarded customer struggles to activate mobile banking and receives no follow-up from the bank. Which strategic-thinking principle has been neglected?
opts: Relationship management as a trusted advisor
questionBank.ans: Ensure easy and effective onboarding
questionBank.exp: Follow-up to ensure seamless integration into the bank's ecosystem, including digital adoption, is the defining feature of the onboarding principle; the scenario shows exactly this step missing.

questionBank.q: A bank analyzes transaction behaviour to offer tailored financial solutions before a customer even asks. Which principle does this represent?
questionBank.ans: Anticipate and solve customer needs
questionBank.exp: Anticipating needs means analyzing behaviour and offering tailored solutions without waiting to be asked — precisely what the scenario describes.

questionBank.q: A customer repeatedly asks the bank for guidance before the bank ever proactively reaches out with tailored suggestions. Which practice would correct this gap?
opts: Analyzing the customer's behaviour and offering tailored solutions unprompted
Waiting for a formal complaint before responding
Reviewing the account only during a scheduled audit
questionBank.ans: Analyzing the customer's behaviour and offering tailored solutions unprompted
questionBank.exp: Anticipating needs means analyzing behaviour and offering tailored solutions without waiting to be asked — described here as the corrective action itself, a distinct angle from Q13's direct-recall framing of the principle's name.

questionBank.q: Encouraging customers to adopt mobile banking, automation tools, and savings plans mainly serves which strategic-thinking principle?
opts: Leverage digital banking for convenience and retention
Relationship management as a trusted advisor
questionBank.ans: Leverage digital banking for convenience and retention
questionBank.exp: This principle explicitly covers encouraging mobile and online banking adoption plus educating customers on automation and savings tools to enhance engagement.

questionBank.q: A customer who rarely visits a branch is taught to use bill-payment automation and a digital savings plan. Which practice does this exemplify?
opts: Monitoring the account for early signs of churn
Educating the customer on automation tools and savings plans to boost engagement
Offering a personalized financial consultation in-branch
Clearly disclosing product terms before sign-up
questionBank.ans: Educating the customer on automation tools and savings plans to boost engagement
questionBank.exp: This practice is the concrete action behind the digital-banking principle: educating customers on automation and savings tools to enhance engagement — phrased as the action itself rather than restating the principle's name (contrast with Q15).

questionBank.q: A banker helps a customer make an informed financial decision rather than simply selling a product, deepening the customer's trust over time. Which principle is this?
opts: Relationship management: be a trusted advisor
questionBank.ans: Relationship management: be a trusted advisor
questionBank.exp: Going beyond selling products to help customers make informed decisions, fostering deeper engagement and loyalty, defines the trusted-advisor principle.

questionBank.q: Which behaviour best distinguishes a trusted-advisor relationship from a purely transactional one?
opts: Processing requests without discussing the customer's goals
Offering personalized advice that fosters trust and deeper engagement
Recommending only the bank's highest-margin product
questionBank.ans: Offering personalized advice that fosters trust and deeper engagement
questionBank.exp: The trusted-advisor principle is defined by personalized advice that fosters trust, contrasted here with purely transactional or self-interested alternatives.

questionBank.q: A bank waits until a customer has already left before attempting to win them back with a special offer. Which principle does this contradict?
questionBank.ans: Prevent attrition: retention over recovery
questionBank.exp: This principle calls for monitoring inactive accounts and re-engaging customers before they leave, making retention preferable to recovery after the fact — the scenario shows the reverse.

questionBank.q: Which of the following is a recommended action under the retention-over-recovery principle?
opts: Reviewing inactive accounts only during annual audits
Monitoring inactive accounts and re-engaging customers proactively
Offering discounts only after a formal complaint
Contacting customers solely through mailed statements
questionBank.ans: Monitoring inactive accounts and re-engaging customers proactively
questionBank.exp: Proactive service, personalized offers, and prompt issue resolution to reduce churn before customers leave is the defined recommended action, unlike the reactive alternatives listed.

questionBank.q: A banker avoids aggressive sales tactics and always clearly explains a loan's terms and conditions. Which principle does this best illustrate?
questionBank.ans: Build lasting trust
questionBank.exp: Clear communication of product terms and avoidance of aggressive sales tactics is precisely how the module defines building lasting trust, since loyalty thrives on honesty.

questionBank.q: Which pair of actions together best build lasting trust with a customer, per the module's guidance?
opts: Clearly communicating terms and avoiding aggressive sales tactics
Maximizing product uptake and minimizing disclosure time
Bundling products without itemizing their terms
Prioritizing speed of sale over accuracy of information
questionBank.ans: Clearly communicating terms and avoiding aggressive sales tactics
questionBank.exp: The module states loyalty thrives on honesty, achieved by clearly communicating product terms and avoiding aggressive sales tactics — the other options describe the opposite behaviours.

questionBank.q: Which sequence correctly orders the stages of the Customer Value Journey from first contact to loyal recommendation?
opts: Engagement, Awareness, Conversion, Advocacy, Excitement and Ascension
Awareness, Engagement, Conversion, Excitement and Ascension, Advocacy
Conversion, Awareness, Engagement, Advocacy, Excitement and Ascension
Awareness, Conversion, Engagement, Advocacy, Excitement and Ascension
questionBank.ans: Awareness, Engagement, Conversion, Excitement and Ascension, Advocacy
questionBank.exp: The Customer Value Journey runs Awareness, Engagement, Conversion (account opening), Excitement and Ascension, then Advocacy, in that order.

questionBank.q: A prospective customer has just heard of a bank for the first time but has taken no further action. Which CVJ stage are they in?
questionBank.ans: Awareness
questionBank.exp: Awareness is the stage where the customer first learns about the bank's services, before any research or interaction with the bank has begun.

questionBank.q: A prospect who has heard of a bank starts researching its fees online and messaging its support chat with questions. Which CVJ stage does this represent?
questionBank.ans: Engagement
questionBank.exp: Engagement is defined as the customer showing interest by researching or interacting with the bank, which is exactly what the researching and messaging describe.

questionBank.q: A customer who has been researching a bank finally applies for a loan and opens an account. Which CVJ stage has just occurred?
questionBank.ans: Conversion
questionBank.exp: Conversion is the stage where the customer takes action, such as opening an account or applying for a loan, following the research done during Engagement.

questionBank.q: After opening an account, a bank runs ongoing campaigns to keep a customer engaged and loyal over time, before that customer ever recommends the bank to others. Which stage is this?
questionBank.ans: Excitement and Ascension
questionBank.exp: Excitement and Ascension is where the bank works to maintain customer loyalty through engagement, positioned between account opening and the customer becoming an advocate.

questionBank.q: A satisfied long-time customer begins recommending the bank to friends and colleagues. Which CVJ stage has this customer reached?
questionBank.ans: Advocacy
questionBank.exp: Advocacy is the final CVJ stage, where the customer recommends the bank to others and becomes a loyal supporter.

questionBank.q: If a bank fails to guide a prospect through each successive stage of the Customer Value Journey, what does the module warn is the likely outcome?
opts: The prospect becomes a passive but loyal customer
The prospect becomes lost, loses interest, or is distracted by another provider
The prospect automatically advances to Advocacy
The prospect reverts permanently to the Awareness stage
questionBank.ans: The prospect becomes lost, loses interest, or is distracted by another provider
questionBank.exp: The module states that without guidance and encouragement at each step, prospects are likely to become lost, lose interest, or be distracted by another product or service.

questionBank.q: Why is the Awareness stage described as critical to a customer's entire journey with a bank?
opts: It is the only stage the bank can measure
If prospects never become aware of the bank, they may never begin the journey toward advocacy
It guarantees conversion regardless of later stages
It replaces the need for a Conversion stage
questionBank.ans: If prospects never become aware of the bank, they may never begin the journey toward advocacy
questionBank.exp: The module states that if potential customers are not aware of the bank or do not recognize its value, they may never begin their journey, let alone become advocates.

questionBank.q: Emeka has just relocated to Lagos and is searching online for guidance on settling in and managing his finances. Which strategic approach specifically targets his location as a newcomer?
opts: Targeted content marketing on settling-in challenges
Local SEO optimized for Lagos-specific searches
Social media engagement on platforms he uses
questionBank.ans: Local SEO optimized for Lagos-specific searches
questionBank.exp: Local SEO is described as strategic specifically because it targets a prospect's specific location, such as optimizing for searches like 'best banks in Lagos for expats' — distinct from the other awareness tactics, which are strategic for different reasons.

questionBank.q: A bank publishes an article titled 'Top 5 Tips for New Arrivals in Lagos' that helps readers regardless of whether they ever open an account. Why is this considered strategic rather than purely promotional?
opts: It targets a specific geographic search term
It provides value beyond just advertising
It builds a direct alliance with another organization
It relies on a demographic-specific social platform
questionBank.ans: It provides value beyond just advertising
questionBank.exp: Targeted content marketing is described as strategic specifically because it provides value beyond just advertising, unlike local SEO (geographic targeting) or partnerships (alliances).

questionBank.q: A bank runs targeted ads on the platforms a tech-savvy newcomer is likely to already use, highlighting its mobile banking and branch network. Which awareness tactic is this?
questionBank.ans: Social media engagement
questionBank.exp: Social media engagement is described as the strategic use of social media to reach a specific demographic, distinct from content marketing's educational value or SEO's geographic focus.

questionBank.q: A bank collaborates with a relocation agency to reach newcomers before they begin searching for a bank on their own. Which awareness tactic is this?
questionBank.ans: Strategic partnerships with relocation services
questionBank.exp: Partnerships are described as a strategic alliance to reach a specific target audience, in this case newcomers, distinct from the other awareness tactics.

questionBank.q: If a bank had already concluded that airline travellers were a profitable market segment, which awareness tactic would most directly reach that specific group before they even start searching for a bank?
opts: Partnerships with organizations serving airline travellers
General content marketing on financial literacy
questionBank.ans: Partnerships with organizations serving airline travellers
questionBank.exp: Partnerships allow direct access to a peer group's channel before individuals begin an independent search, making this the most targeted route to an already-identified segment, echoing the module's own discussion question.

questionBank.q: A bank has made a prospect aware of its services, but the prospect remains unknown to the bank as an individual. What is the bank's next strategic priority at this point?
opts: Capture the prospect's contact details to profile them
Close the branch nearest the prospect's home
Wait for the prospect to become an advocate
questionBank.ans: Capture the prospect's contact details to profile them
questionBank.exp: Once aware, the next challenge is that the bank does not yet know the individual; designing an activity that requires registration is how contact details such as email, phone, and gender are captured for profiling via data analytics.

questionBank.q: Why does the module recommend requiring registration for an activity, even if that activity is offered for free?
opts: To collect personal contact details for customer profiling
To reduce the bank's marketing budget
To satisfy a regulatory reporting requirement
questionBank.ans: To collect personal contact details for customer profiling
questionBank.exp: The stated goal of requiring registration is to collect contact details such as e-mail, phone number, address, gender, and marital status, enabling the bank's data-analytics resources to profile the prospect.

questionBank.q: Once a bank has a new arrival's contact details, it sends messages highlighting transaction-account benefits, easy setup, and mobile-banking features. Which tactic is this?
questionBank.ans: Personalized email marketing
questionBank.exp: Personalized email marketing is described as strategic personalization based on the prospect's likely needs as a new arrival, once their details are in the database.

questionBank.q: A bank showcases quick transfers and bill payments through its mobile app to a tech-savvy prospect. Which tactic does this represent?
opts: User-friendly online and mobile banking demo
questionBank.ans: User-friendly online and mobile banking demo
questionBank.exp: This tactic is described as a strategic focus on the digital experience, a key factor for tech-savvy individuals, distinct from email marketing's personalization or incentives tied to physical visits.

questionBank.q: A bank offers a special welcome package or discount if a new arrival visits a physical branch. Which strategic purpose does the module attach to this tactic?
opts: Building a personal connection through a traditional channel
Profiling the prospect through registration data
questionBank.ans: Building a personal connection through a traditional channel
questionBank.exp: The branch-visit incentive is described as a strategic use of a traditional channel to build a personal connection, distinct from the digital-demo tactic or the data-profiling activity.

questionBank.q: A bank provides a prospect with clear, side-by-side information comparing its offerings against competitors. What strategic purpose does the module assign to this tactic?
opts: Strategic personalization based on likely needs
Strategic use of a traditional channel
Strategic focus on the digital experience
questionBank.ans: Strategic transparency to build trust
questionBank.exp: Comparison tools and information are described as strategic transparency to build trust, distinct from the personalization behind email marketing or the traditional-channel purpose of a branch incentive.

questionBank.q: Which two tactics are most directly aimed at converting an already-aware prospect who is not yet in the bank's database into a profiled contact?
opts: Local SEO and social media engagement
A registration-based activity followed by personalized email marketing
questionBank.ans: A registration-based activity followed by personalized email marketing
questionBank.exp: The registration activity captures contact details for profiling, and the subsequent personalized email marketing then acts on that captured data — the other pairs belong to the earlier, pure-awareness stage instead.

questionBank.q: A newcomer to Lagos is unsure which bank offers the best value and searches for comparisons before deciding. Providing which tool most directly addresses this specific concern?
opts: Comparison tools showing Access Bank's advantages against competitors
A registration-only event for data capture
questionBank.ans: Comparison tools showing Access Bank's advantages against competitors
questionBank.exp: Comparison tools/information directly addresses the prospect's own stated need to weigh offerings, whereas the other tools serve earlier awareness or data-capture purposes rather than side-by-side evaluation.

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the module's four listed Strategic Rationale 1 tactics for building awareness with a newcomer?
questionBank.ans: A branch-visit welcome package
questionBank.exp: Strategic Rationale 1 lists targeted content marketing, local SEO, social media engagement, and partnerships. The branch-visit welcome package belongs instead to Strategic Rationale 2, once the prospect is already being converted.

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the module's four listed Strategic Rationale 2 tactics for converting an aware prospect?
opts: A user-friendly online and mobile banking demo
questionBank.ans: Local SEO for Lagos-specific searches
questionBank.exp: Strategic Rationale 2 lists a registration activity, personalized email marketing, a digital banking demo, a branch-visit incentive, and comparison tools. Local SEO instead belongs to Strategic Rationale 1's earlier awareness-building tactics.

questionBank.q: A prospect is both searching for 'best banks in Lagos for expats' and asking friends for recommendations. Which two tactics respectively address these two behaviours?
opts: Local SEO and social media engagement
Targeted content marketing and comparison tools
Personalized email marketing and branch incentives
questionBank.ans: Local SEO and strategic partnerships
questionBank.exp: Local SEO targets the search-engine behaviour directly, while partnerships with relocation services or expat communities reach the prospect through trusted peer or community channels, matching the friend-recommendation behaviour.

questionBank.q: Both targeted content marketing and comparison tools/information give a prospect helpful information. What distinguishes their strategic roles across the journey?
opts: Comparison tools build awareness value before research begins; content marketing builds transparency once a decision is imminent
Content marketing builds awareness value before research begins; comparison tools build transparency once a decision is imminent
Both operate exclusively once the customer has already opened an account
Both are used only to satisfy regulatory disclosure requirements
questionBank.ans: Content marketing builds awareness value before research begins; comparison tools build transparency once a decision is imminent
questionBank.exp: Content marketing sits in Strategic Rationale 1, providing value during Awareness before the prospect is even in the bank's database, while comparison tools sit in Strategic Rationale 2, providing transparency once the prospect is actively weighing Access Bank against competitors — a sequencing distinction rather than a restatement of Q32's single fact.

questionBank.q: Which statement correctly reflects why the module treats 'Is he likely to be the kind of customer the bank is looking for?' as a key awareness-stage question?
opts: It has no bearing on which channels the bank should use
It helps the bank judge whether a prospect fits its target profile before investing further
It only matters after the Conversion stage
It is answered solely through comparison tools
questionBank.ans: It helps the bank judge whether a prospect fits its target profile before investing further
questionBank.exp: The module lists this question alongside 'how do we know he exists' and 'how can we profile him' as part of assessing a new prospect at the Awareness stage, before committing further marketing investment.

questionBank.q: A bank runs a seven-day discounted-rate 'Green Savings Week' promotion, while separately funding multi-year research into underbanked communities to guide its long-term positioning. Which initiative illustrates marketing strategy rather than strategic marketing?
opts: The seven-day Green Savings Week promotion
questionBank.ans: The seven-day Green Savings Week promotion
questionBank.exp: A short, campaign-specific promotion mirrors the module's own Example-row illustration of marketing strategy (a social-media campaign for a savings account), while sustained, research-driven positioning work mirrors its illustration of strategic marketing.

questionBank.q: A bank's Awareness-stage content addresses a newcomer's settling-in challenges, while its Conversion-stage emails address the newcomer's specific new-arrival banking needs. What do both approaches have in common strategically?
opts: Both rely on the same registration-based data-capture step
Both personalize the message to the prospect's likely situation and needs
Both are executed exclusively through branch visits
Both depend entirely on partnerships with third parties
questionBank.ans: Both personalize the message to the prospect's likely situation and needs
questionBank.exp: Content marketing (Awareness) and personalized email marketing (Conversion) are each described as tailored to the newcomer's likely challenges or needs, even though they operate at different CVJ stages and via different mechanics.

questionBank.q: Which of the following pairs a CVJ stage with a mismatched description?
opts: Awareness — the customer first learns about the bank's services
Engagement — the customer takes action such as opening an account
Conversion — the customer opens an account or applies for a loan
Advocacy — the customer recommends the bank to others
questionBank.ans: Engagement — the customer takes action such as opening an account
questionBank.exp: Taking action such as opening an account describes Conversion, not Engagement. Engagement instead describes the customer researching or interacting with the bank prior to taking that action.

questionBank.q: A bank achieves strong Awareness and Engagement with a prospect but then makes account opening slow and confusing. Which CVJ transition is most directly at risk?
questionBank.ans: Engagement into Conversion
questionBank.exp: Conversion is the stage where the customer takes action, such as opening an account; a slow, confusing process at this point most directly risks losing a prospect between Engagement and Conversion, the two stages already achieved and next in sequence.

questionBank.q: A bank wants to appear near the top of results when a prospect searches for 'best bank card for online transactions.' Which awareness-stage strategy directly addresses this?
questionBank.ans: Digital advertising and SEO
questionBank.exp: Digital advertising and SEO are described as positioning the bank as a top choice when a prospect searches specific terms, distinct from social media presence's role of introducing offerings or influencer marketing's reliance on trusted third parties.

questionBank.q: A bank posts engaging content on Twitter, Instagram, and LinkedIn to introduce a prospect to its offerings before that prospect has searched for anything specific. Which strategy is this?
questionBank.ans: Social media presence
questionBank.exp: Social media presence is described as engaging content on these platforms that can introduce a prospect to the bank's offerings, distinct from SEO's search-triggered positioning.

questionBank.q: A prospect becomes interested in a bank only after a trusted friend and a financial influencer both mention it favourably. Which strategy explains this outcome?
questionBank.ans: Influencer and referral marketing
questionBank.exp: Influencer and referral marketing is described specifically as increasing a prospect's likelihood of interest when a trusted friend or financial influencer mentions the bank.

questionBank.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three effective awareness-stage strategies listed for reaching a prospect who is not yet a customer?
opts: A discounted package offered for visiting a branch in person
questionBank.ans: A discounted package offered for visiting a branch in person
questionBank.exp: The three listed awareness-stage strategies are digital advertising and SEO, social media presence, and influencer and referral marketing. An in-person branch incentive belongs instead to the later Decision-stage tactics.

questionBank.q: An information-seeking newcomer is described as likely to search online, engage with local communities, and look for reliable, convenient financial solutions. What must marketing efforts do as a result, beyond simply reaching him?
opts: Offer educational, engaging content rather than just promotional material
Limit contact to in-branch interactions only
questionBank.ans: Offer educational, engaging content rather than just promotional material
questionBank.exp: The module states marketing must reach the prospect where he is active and offer more than promotional content — it should be educational and engaging to guide him toward an informed decision.

questionBank.q: A prospect is likely to search phrases such as 'best banks in Lagos for newcomers' or 'how to open a bank account in Nigeria.' Which channel and strategic approach pairing matches this behaviour?
opts: WhatsApp groups; participating for brand visibility
Google Search and SEO; optimizing content for localized search ranking
questionBank.ans: Google Search and SEO; optimizing content for localized search ranking
questionBank.exp: The channel table pairs Google Search and SEO specifically with these search phrases, recommending optimized blog and website content for localized SEO ranking.

questionBank.q: A prospect follows financial influencers and industry pages to stay current on financial solutions. Which channel and approach does the module recommend to reach him there?
opts: WhatsApp and Telegram groups; direct messaging
Social media (Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok); targeted ads and influencer collaborations
YouTube and TikTok; short account-setup tutorials
questionBank.ans: Social media (Twitter, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok); targeted ads and influencer collaborations
questionBank.exp: The channel table pairs this following behaviour with social media platforms, recommending targeted ads, influencer collaborations, and engaging content.

questionBank.q: A tech-savvy prospect prefers learning through short, engaging videos rather than reading articles. Which channel does the module recommend, and for what kind of content?
opts: YouTube and TikTok for videos on account setup and navigating banking in Lagos
Google Search for localized blog content
questionBank.ans: YouTube and TikTok for videos on account setup and navigating banking in Lagos
questionBank.exp: The channel table specifically recommends short, engaging videos on YouTube and TikTok for setting up accounts, managing finances, and navigating banking in Lagos, matching the video-preference behaviour described.

questionBank.q: Many Nigerian professionals engage in finance-related chat groups for recommendations before choosing a bank. Which channel and approach addresses this specific behaviour?
opts: WhatsApp and Telegram groups; marketing and participation for brand visibility
questionBank.ans: WhatsApp and Telegram groups; marketing and participation for brand visibility
questionBank.exp: The channel table pairs this chat-group recommendation-seeking behaviour specifically with WhatsApp and Telegram groups, recommending marketing and participation in relevant groups for visibility.

questionBank.q: Which channel-behaviour pairing from the module is mismatched?
opts: Google Search and SEO — searching for how to open a bank account in Nigeria
YouTube and TikTok — engaging in finance-related chat groups for recommendations
Social media — following influencers and industry pages
WhatsApp and Telegram — engaging in finance-related chat groups for recommendations
questionBank.ans: YouTube and TikTok — engaging in finance-related chat groups for recommendations
questionBank.exp: Engaging in finance-related chat groups for recommendations is paired with WhatsApp and Telegram, not YouTube and TikTok, which are instead paired with a preference for video content.

questionBank.q: A bank publishes 'Top 5 Banking Tips for Lagos Newcomers.' What is the stated reason this content type works?
opts: It is the cheapest content format to produce
It provides practical value beyond marketing, making the bank appear helpful and trustworthy
It replaces the need for social media presence
questionBank.ans: It provides practical value beyond marketing, making the bank appear helpful and trustworthy
questionBank.exp: Blog articles of this kind are described as working because they provide practical value beyond just marketing, making the bank appear helpful and trustworthy.

questionBank.q: A bank produces 'How to Budget and Save in Your First Year in Lagos.' Why does the module say this content type works?
opts: It is shareable primarily through billboards
It helps the prospect navigate their financial life while associating the bank with expert advice
It is required for account opening
It substitutes for a dedicated relationship manager
questionBank.ans: It helps the prospect navigate their financial life while associating the bank with expert advice
questionBank.exp: Financial guides of this kind are described as helping the prospect navigate their financial life while associating the bank with expert advice.

questionBank.q: A bank creates 'How to Open a Nigerian Bank Account in 3 Easy Steps' as a visual piece. Why is this content type effective, per the module?
opts: It requires the least strategic planning
It is visually appealing and shareable across social media and WhatsApp groups
It only works for existing customers
It replaces the need for local SEO
questionBank.ans: It is visually appealing and shareable across social media and WhatsApp groups
questionBank.exp: Infographics are described as effective specifically because they are visually appealing and shareable across social media and WhatsApp groups.

questionBank.q: A bank produces 'Best Banking Apps in Nigeria: Which One is Right for You?' as a short clip. Why does the module say this content type works?
opts: It is the least engaging content format available
It is highly engaging and quickly delivers value in an easy-to-digest format
It is only suitable for LinkedIn distribution
It requires no video production resources
questionBank.ans: It is highly engaging and quickly delivers value in an easy-to-digest format
questionBank.exp: Short videos are described as highly engaging, delivering value quickly in an easy-to-digest format, matching this example title.

questionBank.q: Which content type and its stated advantage are correctly matched?
opts: Blog articles — visually appealing and shareable across WhatsApp groups
Financial guides — help the prospect navigate their financial life while associating the bank with expert advice
Infographics — provide practical value beyond just marketing
Short videos — require no distribution strategy
questionBank.ans: Financial guides — help the prospect navigate their financial life while associating the bank with expert advice
questionBank.exp: Financial guides are matched with helping the prospect navigate their financial life while linking the bank to expert advice; the other pairings swap in advantages that belong to different content types.

questionBank.q: A bank wants a prospect to engage with its brand and find value even before ever opening an account. What overarching positioning does the module recommend achieving through content marketing?
opts: Positioning as the cheapest provider in the market
Positioning as an expert in financial literacy
Positioning as the fastest branch network
Positioning as a purely digital-only provider
questionBank.ans: Positioning as an expert in financial literacy
questionBank.exp: The module states the key strategy is to position the bank as an expert in financial literacy, ensuring the prospect finds value in engaging with the brand even before opening an account.

questionBank.q: A prospect is now actively comparing fees, benefits, and mobile-banking experiences across several banks. Which factor-addressing tactic explains a bank's unique benefits directly against competitors?
questionBank.ans: Comparison content

questionBank.q: Which formula correctly calculates Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)?

Total Marketing Spend ÷ Number of New Customers Acquired
Total Marketing Spend × Number of New Customers Acquired
Total Marketing Spend – Number of New Customers Acquired

(Average Revenue per Customer × Average Customer Lifespan) – CAC
Average Revenue per Customer ÷ Average Customer Lifespan
(Average Revenue per Customer – Average Customer Lifespan) × CAC

questionBank.exp: CLTV is defined as (Average Revenue per Customer × Average Customer Lifespan) minus CAC, not a sum, a division, or a reordered formula.
